mcp_server.apps.confirmMessage: {app} will lose access to this workspace at once. To use it again, connect it again.
mcp_server.apps.disconnectError: The app could not be disconnected.
mcp_server.apps.subtitle: AI apps you connected to this workspace with a sign-in. Disconnecting one stops it at once.
mcp_server.apps.title: Connected apps
mcp_server.consent.actsAsYou: It acts as you, and never with more than your access in this workspace.
mcp_server.consent.disconnect: You can disconnect it at any time in Connected apps.
mcp_server.consent.failed: The app could not be connected.
mcp_server.consent.loadError: This request could not be checked.
mcp_server.consent.readOnly: It can read what you can read through the workspace's AI tools. It cannot change anything.
mcp_server.consent.title: Connect {app} to this workspace?
mcp_server.consent.write: It can read what you can read, and create and change records you may create and change, through the workspace's AI tools. It cannot delete anything.
mcp_server.firewallHoneytoken.decoy_toke: An access token shaped like a real one that no app was ever given. Anyone presenting it on an MCP server holds a stolen or planted copy.
mcp_server.permission.mcp_server_connect: Lets an API key (or, later, a connected AI app) reach the workspace's MCP servers. Each tool still needs its own module permission, held by the key and by its holder.
mcp_server.permission.mcp_server_setting: Switch MCP access for the workspace on or off and switch single tools off (Settings → MCP).
mcp_server.settings.mcpAllowedClientHost: Hosts of AI apps that may connect with a sign-in (OAuth) beside the known ones (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code, GitHub), one per line, for example tools.example.com.
mcp_server.settings.mcpDisabledTools.des: Tools no one in this workspace may use, one per line as server/tool, for example tasks/get_task. The list of servers and tools is at /api/mcp.
mcp_server.settings.mcpEnabled.descripti: AI apps (Claude, Cursor, VS Code and others) may connect to this workspace with an API key that holds "Connect MCP clients". Each tool still needs its own permission, held by the key and by its owner. Off by default.
mcp_server.settings.mcpEnabled.label: Let MCP clients connect
mcp_server.settings.subtitle: Whether AI apps may connect to this workspace, and which tools they may not use
mcp_server.settings.title: MCP
mcp_server.settingsLink.desc: Let AI apps connect with an API key, and switch tools off
mcp_server.settingsLink.title: MCP
